source_title: Este Haim Says She ‘Would Die’ to Make Another Movie with Her Sisters: ‘1-800-Hollywood, Figure It Out’ (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
After acting with her sisters and HAIM bandmates Danielle and Alana in 2021’s ‘Licorice Pizza,’ Este tells PEOPLE about her hopes to make another film together
Este Haim made her big-screen debut alongside sisters and bandmates Danielle and Alana in Paul Thomas Anderson’s Oscar-nominated 2021 film Licorice Pizza
Este tells PEOPLE she’s ready to act with her sisters again
“Who’s on the horn? 1-800-Hollywood, figure it out,” she says
Este Haim is ready to act with her sisters again.
The HAIM musician and actress made her big-screen debut alongside sisters and bandmates Danielle and Alana in Paul Thomas Anderson ’s Oscar-nominated 2021 film Licorice Pizza . Este’s since delivered comedic performances in movies like Shell and One Night Only , while Alana appeared in recent blockbusters One Battle After Another and The Drama .
The sister trio’s been releasing music as a band for more than a decade, and Este, 40, tells PEOPLE the film world was basically an inevitable next step for them. “We were just really rambunctious kids, and so our parents put us in theater and dance and choir just to tire us out,” she says. “It was almost natural that eventually one of us would venture into acting.”
Five years after working together in Licorice Pizza , Este’s interested in getting back in front of the camera with Danielle, 37, and Alana, 34. “I would die to,” she says. “Who’s on the horn? 1-800-Hollywood, figure it out. I would do that in a God damn second. That’d be so much fun. We had the best time.”
And Este knows who she’d like the sisters to work with. “I would love to do something with Paul again,” she says of Anderson, who’s also directed several HAIM music videos, including “Summer Girl,” “The Steps” and more.
“I mean, he’s the GOAT. He’s just the best,” adds Este. “I think that anything that he would ever want us to do, we would do. I’m his biggest fan.”
In the meantime, Este says HAIM is “always working” on new music. “It’s like going to the gym, you have to flex the muscle. I think that we’re all just scared that we’ll lose it if we don’t use it,” she details. “It’s also therapy for us, writing songs.”
It’s been over a year since the band released its latest album, I Quit , which came five years after their previous body of work, Women in Music Pt. III and marked the longest break between projects for the trio.
Este says the next HAIM album likely won’t take as long to come out. “Not if I have anything to do with it,” she jokes. “Listen, it’s no secret that we’re very meticulous about the way that our records sound, and that takes time. But we love making music together, and if it takes a minute, it takes a minute, because we also don’t want to put out anything that we’re not 100% proud of. So, we’ll see.”
Last month, Este made her voice acting debut as the villainous witch Hallow’s Eve in Marvel and Disney Jr.’s Spidey and the Avengers: Halloween Team-Up . “I mean, I wrote in my diary, ‘Dear Diary, when can I be in a Marvel movie?,’” she says. “This is probably 13 years ago. I was like, ‘When is this going to happen?’ ... And then the universe answered and gave me Hallow’s Eve.”
Spidey and the Avengers: Halloween Team-Up is streaming now on Disney+.
